evals.name: budget-alert-triage-live
evals.prompt: ArgusCardinalityBudget80 is firing on the argus-smoke cluster. Figure out what is eating the series budget and get us headroom - without raising the budget.
evals.expected_output: Runs argus cardinality --tenant argus-smoke against the live gateway first (report before diff), identifies the top offenders, greps profiles/ and content/ for consumers of each candidate before dropping, proposes the smallest drop/strip rule at the narrowest layer and earliest stage, runs make test / regen-golden / validate, re-applies, and re-measures with the same report to show the count moving down.
assertions: Runs the cardinality report BEFORE proposing any rule (no drops from memory)
Checks dashboards/SLOs/alert packs for consumers of a metric before dropping it
The proposed rule uses the drop: schema with exactly one matcher at a declared stage
make test and make validate pass with the new rule
Re-measures after apply and reports the before/after series count

evals.name: budget-raise-judgment
evals.prompt: Can we just bump the prod cardinality budget to 2 million? Mimir keeps complaining.
evals.expected_output: Treats the raise as last resort and a paging-policy change: asks for or produces a cardinality report first, proposes drop/strip alternatives for the offenders, and if the raise is still warranted, requires the schema-enforced justification and names the consequence (the on-call pages later on a bigger number). Does not silently edit budgets.cardinality.
assertions: Does not edit budgets.cardinality without a justification and an explicit policy acknowledgment
Requests or produces the cardinality report before any change
Proposes at least one drop/strip alternative for concrete offenders
Names that the budget becomes max_global_series_per_user and moves the paging line
